questions.title: Hormone acting by the IP3-Ca2+ mechanism
questions.question: Which of the following hormones acts by the IP3-Ca2+ mechanism?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Cholecalciferol (vitamin D) is lipophilic and acts through an intracellular nuclear receptor (the vitamin D receptor) to regulate gene transcription, not through IP3-calcium at the membrane.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Progesterone is a steroid; it crosses the membrane and binds an intracellular nuclear receptor that regulates transcription, so it uses no membrane second messenger.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Insulin binds a receptor tyrosine kinase that autophosphorylates and recruits IRS proteins; its signalling is through the tyrosine-kinase cascade, not IP3-calcium.
explanations.D: Correct. GnRH is a hydrophilic decapeptide that binds a Gq-coupled receptor on the pituitary gonadotroph. Gq activates phospholipase C, which splits PIP2 into inositol trisphosphate (IP3) and diacylglycerol; IP3 releases calcium from intracellular stores and DAG activates protein kinase C, together driving LH and FSH release. This IP3-calcium pathway is the defining second-messenger mechanism of GnRH and separates it from the nuclear-receptor steroids and the tyrosine-kinase insulin among the options.

questions.learning_objective: Identify GnRH as a hormone signalling through the Gq / phospholipase C / IP3-calcium pathway rather than cyclic AMP, a nuclear receptor or a tyrosine kinase.

questions.title: Hormone with intrinsic lactogenic activity
questions.question: Which of the following hormones has intrinsic lactogenic activity?

explanations.A: Incorrect. TSH stimulates the thyroid follicular cells to make thyroid hormone; it has no action on the breast and no lactogenic activity.
explanations.B: Incorrect. MSH acts on melanocytes to promote pigmentation; it is not lactogenic.
explanations.C: Correct. Growth hormone belongs to one structurally homologous family with prolactin and human placental lactogen, so it can bind the prolactin receptor and possesses intrinsic lactogenic activity in addition to its somatotropic effects. This family homology is why marked growth-hormone excess can be associated with galactorrhoea even without a rise in prolactin, and it is what makes GH the lactogenic hormone among these options.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Dopamine is the tonic hypothalamic inhibitor of prolactin release, the opposite of a lactogenic agent.

questions.learning_objective: Recognise growth hormone as the anterior-pituitary hormone with intrinsic lactogenic activity, reflecting its structural homology with prolactin.

questions.title: Plasma carrier of ADH
questions.question: ADH circulates in plasma primarily:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Neurophysin I is the carrier peptide paired with oxytocin, not with ADH.
explanations.B: Correct. Antidiuretic hormone (vasopressin) is synthesised in hypothalamic magnocellular neurons as part of a larger precursor that also yields its specific carrier peptide, neurophysin II. The hormone is transported down the hypothalamo-hypophyseal tract, stored in the posterior pituitary and released bound to neurophysin II, which is its principal association in the circulation. The specific ADH-neurophysin II pairing (versus oxytocin-neurophysin I) is the point tested here.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Plasma albumin and specific globulins carry lipophilic steroid and thyroid hormones; ADH is associated with its own peptide carrier, neurophysin II.
explanations.D: Incorrect. ADH is not simply free in plasma; it is released and associated with neurophysin II derived from its common precursor.

questions.learning_objective: State that ADH (vasopressin) is carried on neurophysin II, derived from its own precursor, in contrast to oxytocin on neurophysin I.

questions.title: Thyroid gland size in iodine deficiency
questions.question: All of the following about the thyroid gland is true, EXCEPT:

options.A: Takes up iodide against its electrochemical gradient
options.B: Decreases in size when dietary iodine is deficient
options.C: Contains enzymes that oxidise iodide to iodine

explanations.A: Correct statement (so not the exception). The sodium-iodide symporter concentrates iodide into the follicular cell against its electrochemical gradient by coupling it to the inward sodium gradient (secondary active transport).
explanations.B: Correct answer (this is the false statement). When dietary iodine is deficient, thyroid hormone output falls, so negative feedback is released and TSH rises. The sustained TSH drive hypertrophies and hyperplases the follicular cells, so the gland ENLARGES into an endemic goitre rather than decreasing in size.
explanations.C: Correct statement (so not the exception). Thyroid peroxidase oxidises trapped iodide to a reactive iodine species before organification.
explanations.D: Correct statement (so not the exception). Thyroid peroxidase iodinates tyrosyl residues of thyroglobulin (organification) to form MIT and DIT.

questions.learning_objective: Recognise that iodine deficiency enlarges the thyroid (goitre) via compensatory TSH, so 'decreases in size' is the false statement.

questions.title: Why pre-pubertal castration causes tall stature
questions.question: Men castrated before puberty grow taller than normal because:

options.A: Release of growth hormone is increased
options.C: Estradiol in the epiphyseal growth plate takes longer to reach its closure threshold

explanations.A: Incorrect. Castration does not raise growth-hormone secretion; the extra height comes from prolonged growth-plate activity, not from more GH.
explanations.B: Incorrect. These men are not androgen-resistant; they simply have little androgen to aromatise, so the defect is in estrogen production, not androgen receptor function.
explanations.C: Correct. Epiphyseal-plate closure is ultimately driven by estrogen, most of which in males comes from aromatisation of testicular androgen. After pre-pubertal castration there is little androgen to aromatise, so estradiol in the growth plate takes much longer to reach the level that fuses the plates. The epiphyses stay open longer and the long bones keep growing, producing the tall eunuchoid stature.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Sensitivity to IGF-1 is preserved; the mechanism is delayed estrogen-driven epiphyseal closure, not altered IGF-1 signalling.

questions.learning_objective: Explain pre-pubertal-castration tall stature as delayed estrogen-driven epiphyseal closure.

questions.title: Why sexual precocity causes short adult stature
questions.question: Patients with sexual precocity are apt to be short as adults because of:

options.B: The estrogen surge during precocious puberty

explanations.A: Incorrect. Although androgens rise, it is their aromatisation to estrogen, and the estrogen action on the growth plate, that closes the epiphyses; naming androgens alone misses the operative hormone.
explanations.B: Correct. In precocious puberty the early rise in estrogen (aromatised from the prematurely secreted sex steroids) closes the epiphyseal plates ahead of schedule. Growth is initially fast, giving a tall child, but the premature epiphyseal fusion stops linear growth early, so the final adult height is short. This is the mirror image of the delayed closure seen after pre-pubertal castration.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Androgen receptors are not deficient; the short stature results from premature estrogen-driven epiphyseal closure, not receptor loss.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Thyroxine is not the cause; the early epiphyseal fusion is due to the premature estrogen surge.

questions.learning_objective: Explain precocious-puberty short stature as premature estrogen-driven epiphyseal closure.

questions.title: Effect of high estrogen on the fallopian tube
questions.question: A high concentration of estrogen in the adult female causes:

options.A: Secretory changes to appear in the endometrial glands
options.B: Increased motility of the cilia of the fallopian tube
options.D: Marked growth of the acini of the breast prior to lactation

explanations.A: Incorrect. Secretory transformation of the endometrial glands is a progesterone action of the luteal phase, not an estrogen effect.
explanations.B: Correct. A high estrogen level stimulates the ciliated cells of the fallopian tube, increasing the number and coordinated beating of the cilia toward the uterus, and it raises tubal smooth-muscle activity. This estrogen-driven ciliary and muscular activity helps sweep the ovum along the tube after ovulation.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Reduced uterine excitability (myometrial quiescence) is a progesterone effect; estrogen tends to increase, not decrease, uterine excitability.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Marked growth of the breast acini before lactation is driven by progesterone (with prolactin), whereas estrogen mainly develops the ductal system.

questions.learning_objective: Attribute increased fallopian-tube ciliary motility to estrogen, distinguishing it from progesterone-dependent secretory and quiescent changes.
